findings.title: Correct the claimed Authorization forwarding under IAM auth
findings.body: AgentCore permits Authorization in requestHeaderAllowlist only when a custom JWT authorizer is configured. Without that authorizer, the control plane rejects the runtime create/update; it does not deploy an IAM-authenticated runtime that forwards unchecked Authorization headers. The new explanation therefore describes an impossible deployment state and incorrectly presents it as the rationale for verification inside the agent.

findings.title: Check that the verifier is called, not merely mentioned
findings.body: VERIFIER is already present in the import statement, so this assertion passes if the entrypoint stops calling it. For example, replacing the new assignment with user_id = context.identity.sub leaves both this test and the placeholder-assignment test green while restoring unverified identity handling. The new guard consequently does not enforce its stated authentication invariant.

other_major.title: Catch failures when MCP tools are loaded, not just when the client is constructed
other_major.body: The try block only constructs and appends an MCPClient. Its transport factory is lazy: token retrieval, connection establishment, and tool discovery occur when Strands loads the client, outside this try block. Consequently, an unreachable Gateway or a token-vault failure fails the request instead of continuing without Gateway tools as intended. The existing catch covers configuration-time failures but not the principal outage scenarios it claims to handle.

hits.title: Simulate the configured model resources instead of a generic ARN
hits.body: When agents.allowed_models is configured, the role permits exact model and inference-profile ARNs rather than every foundation model. The fabricated anthropic.claude ARN therefore returns implicitDeny even with the guardrail context, making deploy.sh verify fail on a correctly hardened deployment and incorrectly report that inference is bricked. Resolve the configured model and simulate its actual resource ARNs, including the inference profile and destination foundation-model resources where applicable.

other_major.title: Validate guardrail compatibility after resolving configuration overrides
other_major.body: The compatibility validator only checks the manifest, while this call uses the effective environment/context settings. For example, a valid security-focused manifest combined with AGENT_PATTERN=claude-sdk-agent passes validation but deploys the inference deny onto an agent that cannot attach a guardrail, causing every inference to fail. This affects the documented environment-variable customization path, not just raw CDK context users. Reject the incompatible combination after resolving both require_guardrails and agent_pattern, or enforce it in RuntimeStack, and test the override case.

findings.title: Gate the guardrail check on the runtime footprint
findings.body: A federated platform account deliberately has no runtime stacks, but enabling require_guardrails still schedules this check. check_guardrail_enforcement.py unconditionally looks up the orchestrator runtime role, so verification fails with a missing-role error for a valid platform-account deployment. Only schedule this orchestrator-specific check when runtime-orchestrator is in suffixes, and add a federated-platform test with the flag enabled.

hits.title: Distinguish missing secrets from failed secret checks
hits.body: Every unsuccessful describe-secret call is reported as a missing secret, while the underlying error is discarded. Successful STS authentication does not imply secretsmanager:DescribeSecret permission, so a valid caller with insufficient permissions will receive an incorrect diagnosis and a create-secret recommendation even when the secret exists. Throttling and connectivity failures produce the same result. Capture the AWS error, report 'missing' only for ResourceNotFoundException, and report other failures as an unsuccessful or inconclusive check.

other_major.title: Distinguish the proposed migration from current deployment behavior
other_major.body: The plan says agents.pattern is ignored and the runtime image comes from migration.source, but this PR deliberately leaves app.py and the runtime stacks unchanged and defers consumption of MIGRATION_* to M2. Consequently, deploying the newly updated migration preset still deploys the framework-selected runtime rather than the declared customer container. The plan gives operators a false assurance about what a subsequent deployment will run.

hits.title: Restore the source image's runtime user after installation
hits.body: The Dockerfile switches to root to install dependencies but never switches back. Consequently, both the adapter and the customer's original command run as root even when the source image explicitly configured an unprivileged user. This silently removes an existing security control and gives compromised customer code greater privileges inside the container; documenting the deviation does not preserve that control.

other_major.title: Quote the source-build status message to avoid a shell syntax error
other_major.body: The unquoted parentheses in `echo Building customer image from source (linux/arm64)...` are shell syntax in both sh and bash. CodeBuild fails on this command before building the customer image, so the build-from-source migration path cannot deploy.

other_major.title: Parse complete SSE events rather than yielding each data line
other_major.body: SSE permits multiple `data:` lines in one event; those lines must be joined with newlines and dispatched only at the blank-line event boundary. This implementation yields each line independently, turning a valid multiline event into multiple events and potentially splitting a JSON payload into invalid fragments. The current test covers only single-line events, so it does not catch the corruption.

hits.title: Treat the no-importers ValidationError as a successful handoff
hits.body: When Observability is the last consumer, the successful literal-ARN deployment leaves the export with no importers. CloudFormation list-imports then fails with ValidationError stating that the export is not imported by any stack; it does not return an empty list. This branch treats that expected result as fatal, so the normal handoff exits before replacing the Runtime. The earlier discovery call has the same problem on retries. The regression mock returns 'None' instead of the actual service error and therefore misses this failure.

other_major.title: Recover pending Observability rebinds on targeted retries
other_major.body: The rebind is gated solely by an in-process marker that resets to zero on every invocation. If Runtime replacement succeeds but the rebind fails or the process is interrupted, retrying the same targeted Runtime deployment discovers that current_generation equals target_generation and returns without setting this marker. The rebind is consequently skipped and the command can report success while Observability remains pinned to the deleted Runtime ARN. An interruption after the literal handoff but before replacement similarly loses the marker once discovery finds no Observability importer. This contradicts the advertised resumable targeted deployment flow.
